key_insight: Separating compliance damage from the phase field lets sharp cohesive cracks emerge naturally at finite phase-field length while preserving a continuous phase field.
engineering_relevance: The formulation supports fracture simulation under large deformation and rotation, with independently prescribed bulk material behavior and mixed-mode traction–separation laws.
method: Introduce independent compliance-damage, crack-strain, and reference-normal fields.
Use a rank-one additive split of the deformation gradient to represent crack separation.
Couple bulk deformation, separation, and crack-plane rotation through minimum potential energy.
evidence_signal: One-dimensional energy comparisons favor concentrated cracks; 2D and 3D examples test large stretches, rotations, and complex crack paths, with near-tip stress closely matching an analytical 1/r asymptotic solution outside the cohesive zone.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish mesh-convergence requirements or computational cost for resolving concentrated damage and the additional independent fields.
paper_title: A variational phase-field theory of cohesive fracture at finite deformation
